clue.text: Female member reversing cart in part of grange

parts.note: an arm is a member, a limb of the body

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the word for a cart from back to front

parts.note: a dray is a low flat cart used by brewers

explanation.surface: A woman backing a cart into part of a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a farm with its buildings, and the enclosed yard round the barns is one part of it.

clue.text: Compulsion to line up carrying uniform

indicators.note: carrying means the line-up word holds the uniform letter inside it

parts.note: soldiers dress when they line up in straight ranks
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Being forced to fall in on parade while wearing uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is pressure or threats forcing someone to act, a form of compulsion.

clue.text: Immense good at first relating to good eating

indicators.note: at first places the letter for good at the front of the word for immense

parts.note: astronomical means immense, vast in scale

explanation.surface: Praise for a huge feast that's tasty from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomical is the adjective of gastronomy, the art and enjoyment of fine food.

clue.text: Oddly fertile — and lacking a mate?

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word fertile
lacking means the word and loses the letter a

explanation.surface: Someone fertile but without a partner, which seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes F, R, I, E from fertile; 'lacking' removes A from AND, leaving ND.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate in everyday speech is a pal or companion, the same as a close companion.

clue.text: Harps do badly in the end playing an emotional piece

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of harps do are played about with, rearranged
in the end takes the final letter of badly

explanation.surface: Harpists performing poorly but finally playing a moving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' looks like the anagram signal, but 'in the end' takes its Y; 'playing' rearranges HARPSDO into RHAPSOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free-flowing musical composition full of strong feeling.

clue.text: Drink a quiet composer mostly served in company

indicators.note: served in means the following letters are placed inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: mostly means the composer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Giacomo Puccini was the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A cup of something enjoyed in company with a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the composer's final I; 'quiet' is P because piano is the musical direction for soft, and 'served in' places everything inside the company letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappuccino is an espresso coffee topped with frothed milk, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Fast? For Nancy it's slow

definitions.meaning: the Christian period of fasting before Easter
Nancy is a French city, and the French word for slow is spelt this way

explanation.surface: Puzzling over whether something is quick or slow.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name but is the city in eastern France, so it signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The forty days before Easter are traditionally a fast, and French lent means slow.

clue.text: Way the old viewed a painful swelling?

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: How people long ago regarded a sore lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed, sore lump on the edge of an eyelid.

clue.text: Ill-feeling about concerns involving rogues

indicators.note: about means the word for ill-feeling goes around the word for concerns

parts.note: pique is resentment or ill-feeling
cares are worries or concerns

explanation.surface: Resentment over worries about criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: A picaresque novel follows the adventures of a roguish hero, so the word means involving rogues.

clue.text: Sweetener from old Greek territory — less common, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as they would be said, not as spelt

parts.note: a deme was a township of ancient Attica, and rarer means less common

explanation.surface: A sweetener imported from an ancient Greek region, less common, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent DEME plus RARER is said just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a light brown cane sugar, used to sweeten coffee and baking.

clue.text: Articulate person who swears, seeing indicator on screen

indicators.note: articulate as a verb means to say out loud, so the words are spoken

parts.note: a curser is someone who curses or swears

explanation.surface: A well-spoken swearer spotted by a marker on a monitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursor is the movable pointer on a computer display showing where input will go.

clue.text: Person in Mr Tulliver's position no one rejected — a corker!

parts.note: Mr Tulliver is the miller in George Eliot's The Mill on the Floss, so he is someone in a mill

indicators.note: rejected means the letters for no and one are turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Praise for Mr Tulliver after he refused nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A corker is an outstanding person or thing, someone exceptional, rarer than most.

clue.text: Primate keeping last of flock in bread

indicators.note: keeping means the bread word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: bread is slang for money

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of flock

explanation.surface: An ape holding onto the last bit of a sheep-feeding loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey is one of the primates, the order that includes apes and humans.

clue.text: Study English, absorbing information about traitor

indicators.note: absorbing means the study word takes in the next letters

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: about means the slang word for information is turned round

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A student of English who has learned about a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' is a British sense, as in reading law at university; 'about' turns the slang word round to NEG before 'absorbing' puts it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or side, so it is a turncoat, one who betrays.

clue.text: State raising show for one US city

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to air something is to show it publicly
eg, for example, means for one
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A nation putting on a show for an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns AIREGLA upside down in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a sovereign North African country, and state here means country.

clue.text: Eg great painting of plant in entrance to Maiden Castle?

indicators.note: entrance to takes the first letter of Maiden

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower
the castle, or rook, is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A fine picture of a flower at the gate of Maiden Castle, the Iron Age hillfort in Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is an outstanding work of art, and a great painting is one example.

clue.text: Bitter inspector finally given place in a detective force

indicators.note: given place in means the next letter is put inside a CID

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of inspector

explanation.surface: A resentful inspector at last given a job in the detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and bitter, in taste or smell or in temper.

clue.text: Ancient coins in a dire transmogrification

indicators.note: a transmogrification is a strange transformation, so the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: Old money undergoing a dreadful transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Denarii, plural of denarius, were silver coins of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Keys supplied with less luxurious-sounding carriage

parts.note: D and E are musical keys

indicators.note: sounding means the word for less luxurious is as it is said

parts.note: meaner means poorer, less luxurious

explanation.surface: A poorer coach supplied with musical keys.
explanation.walkthrough: Carriage looks like a vehicle, but it means bearing; the non-rhotic MEANER is said like the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means how one holds and conducts oneself, one's bearing or manner.

clue.text: Legendary flyer taking up French horn?

indicators.note: taking up in a down answer means reading the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: cor is French for horn

explanation.surface: A mythical bird learning to play the French horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant bird of Arabian myth, seen in the Sinbad stories.

clue.text: Sultan's son and daughter abandoned by character in panto

definitions.note: read as Sultan is, so the definition is the sultan himself

indicators.note: abandoned by means the daughter's letter is left out of the panto hero

parts.note: Aladdin is a stock hero of British Christmas pantomime

explanation.surface: A sultan's children deserted by a pantomime figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families; 'abandoned by' takes a D from ALADDIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century Muslim ruler of Egypt and Syria who fought the crusaders.

clue.text: Seven girls father initially abandoned, looking after number one

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters are let loose
initially takes the first letter of father

explanation.surface: A father deserting seven daughters early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' supplies F, mixed with SEVENGIRLS by 'abandoned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after number one is an idiom for putting oneself first, acting purely selfishly.

clue.text: Second man extremely choosy about suitable military rank

indicators.note: about means the second man goes around the word for suitable

parts.note: Cain, son of Adam, was the second man in the Bible
apt means suitable

indicators.note: extremely takes the outer letters of choosy

explanation.surface: An officer fussily choosing a fitting rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain was born after Adam, the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Captaincy is the rank or post of captain, an officer grade in the army.

clue.text: Musical shake? Lot more wobbly!

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Exclaiming over a quavering note, far more shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a rapid quivering repetition of a note in music, a vibrating effect.

clue.text: Attractive person mishandled her car, eating up miles

indicators.note: eating up means the rearranged letters take in the miles letter
mishandled means the letters of her car are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smooth operator who wrecked her car while covering lots of miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mishandled' turns HERCAR into CHARER, and 'eating up' puts M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmer is someone appealing and delightful, a person with charm.

clue.text: Posh bloke outside at present — not admitted

indicators.note: outside means the posh bloke goes round the word for at present

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
Ned is a man's name, so any bloke
now means at present

explanation.surface: An upper-class man currently shut outside.
explanation.definitionFit: If nobody owns something, nobody admits it is theirs: unacknowledged, disowned.

clue.text: Mark made by stripy animal crossing lake?

indicators.note: crossing means the animal spans the letter for lake

parts.note: a coon is a raccoon, with a ringed tail

explanation.surface: A trail left by a striped creature going across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark made of two dots one above the other.

clue.text: Regularly met, like a hoofed mammal

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of met like

explanation.surface: Often seen, as a hoofed animal is.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk is a large deer, and deer are hoofed mammals.
